_provenance.why_this_file_exists: bettor_live_read reported NO_SETTLEMENT_PRICE_IN_RESPONSE and CLOSED_BUT_NO_REPORTED_OR_CONVERGED_OUTCOME for this market. Both were OUR parser's verdicts. listing_market.question: Who will win in the upcoming baseball event Arizona Diamondbacks vs Colorado Rockies scheduled for September 24, 2026 at 7:10 PM UTC?
listing_market.description: This market will settle to the winner of the Arizona Diamondbacks vs Colorado Rockies MLB game scheduled for 2026-09-24 at 3:10PM ET. Extra innings are included if played. If the game is delayed, postponed, or suspended and not rescheduled to a date within two weeks of the originally scheduled date, the market will settle to the last fair market price. Outcome sourced from MLB.

_description_correction.what_was_here: This market settles on the final result of the game, including any extra innings. If the game is abandoned or postponed and never completed the market is void and stakes are returned.
_description_correction.what_is_here_now_and_where_it_came_from: the venue's own `description` for this slug, read live through bettor_venue_settlement_probe._terms_read in command-verify run 36170600524, job 108188921560, and independently measured at 380 characters by the same probe's field_shapes in run 36162992347 at 16:51Z
_description_correction.why_it_was_corrected: the previous value said the market is VOID and STAKES ARE RETURNED when a game is abandoned. The venue says the market settles to the LAST FAIR MARKET PRICE. That is different cash, and a settlement conclusion was drawn from the wrong text and reported to management as the venue's position
_description_correction.what_is_NOT_established: why the two differ. This file's _provenance claims a verbatim capture of every field the parser reads, and the live field was already 380 characters when measured at 16:51Z the same day. So either the capture was not verbatim for this field or the venue changed its template between 13:08Z and 16:51Z. No evidence held here decides which, and nothing in the repository now depends on the old value
_description_correction.the_other_fields: settlement_response and the payout-bearing listing fields are unchanged. The parser behaviour they pin -- an authoritative settlement value under its own key, outcomePrices as a JSON-encoded string -- was verified against production twice and is not in question here
